Fictional spacecraft.Heart of Gold: Heart of Gold, from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, runs on the Infinite Improbability Drive.
Fictional spacecraft.Galactica: Galactica is a battlestar leading a fleet of survivors in Battlestar Galactica, in search of Earth.
Fictional spacecraft.Planet Express Ship: The Planet Express Ship is Futurama's delivery craft, and it's piloted by Leela.
Fictional spacecraft.Event Horizon: Event Horizon is the ship in the 1997 horror film that returns from a trip through a dimension of hell.
Fictional spacecraft.Rocinante: The Rocinante is the ship in The Expanse, named for Don Quixote's horse.
Fictional spacecraft.X-wing: The X-wing is the Rebel fighter in Star Wars, with wings that open in an X for attack.
Fictional spacecraft.TARDIS: The TARDIS is a time machine that looks like a British police box and is bigger on the inside.
Fictional spacecraft.Sputnik: Sputnik 1, launched in 1957, was the first artificial satellite, and it started the space race; it was real.
Fictional spacecraft.Vostok 1: Vostok 1 carried Yuri Gagarin, the first human in space, on April 12, 1961, a real flight.
Fictional spacecraft.Apollo 13: Apollo 13 was a real 1970 mission, with an exploded oxygen tank, and the crew returned safely.
Fictional spacecraft.Voyager 2: Voyager 2 is a real probe launched in 1977, and the only one to visit Uranus and Neptune.
Fictional spacecraft.Hubble: The Hubble Space Telescope is a real telescope, in orbit since 1990.
Fictional spacecraft.Skylab: Skylab was a real US space station, which fell back in 1979.
Fictional spacecraft.Mir: Mir was a real Soviet space station that orbited for 15 years until 2001.
Fictional spacecraft.Cassini: Cassini was a real probe that explored Saturn from 2004 until its plunge into the planet in 2017.
Fictional spacecraft.New Horizons: New Horizons is a real probe that flew past Pluto in 2015.
Fictional spacecraft.Soyuz: Soyuz is a real Russian spacecraft, in use since the 1960s, and still ferries crews.
Fictional spacecraft.Challenger: Challenger was a real space shuttle, lost in 1986 shortly after launch.
Fictional spacecraft.Friendship 7: Friendship 7 carried John Glenn, the first American to orbit Earth, in 1962, and it was a real capsule.

Hand emoji.Thumbs up: One of the most-used emoji; in parts of the Middle East and West Africa the gesture can be rude.
Hand emoji.Waving hand: It's used for hello and goodbye; it has been in Unicode since 2010.
Hand emoji.Clapping hands: Skin-tone options arrived in 2015, letting people have emoji that reflected them.
Hand emoji.Raised fist: Linked to protest and solidarity, and to the Black Power salutes at the 1968 Olympics.
Hand emoji.Folded hands: Can mean prayer, thanks or a high five; in Japan it originally meant 'please' or 'thank you'.
Hand emoji.OK hand: A circle with thumb and forefinger; considered rude in some countries, such as Brazil.
Hand emoji.Crossed fingers: A wish for luck, perhaps rooted in early Christians; in Vietnam it has a vulgar meaning.
Hand emoji.Call me hand: Thumb and pinky extended like a phone; in Hawaii a similar gesture is the 'shaka'.
Hand emoji.Pinching hand: Added in 2020 to show something tiny, and quickly became a meme about small amounts.
Hand emoji.Handshake: Since 2021 you can pick a different skin tone for each hand in this emoji.
Hand emoji.Victory hand: The V sign for peace or victory; Winston Churchill popularized it in World War II.
Hand emoji.Raised hand: The same hand serves as a high five and a 'stop' sign, depending on context.
Hand emoji.Writing hand: From the old Dingbats set, it has existed in Unicode since the early 1990s.
Hand emoji.Ear: An ear is a body part, not a hand; each human ear contains three tiny bones.
Hand emoji.Nose: A body part, not a hand; smell is the sense most closely linked to memory.
Hand emoji.Eye: Human eyes hold roughly 120 million rods and 6 million cones, but the eye isn't a hand.
Hand emoji.Tongue: Taste buds renew every week or two, but the tongue is not a hand.
Hand emoji.Brain: The brain is about 2 percent of body weight but uses roughly 20 percent of the body's energy.
Hand emoji.Bone: Adults have 206 bones, and a single hand has 27 of them.
Hand emoji.Foot: Two feet hold about a quarter of the body's bones, but a foot is not a hand.
Hand emoji.Mouth: A mouth can make up to about a liter of saliva a day.
Hand emoji.Leg: The femur in the leg is the longest and strongest bone in the body.
Hand emoji.Lips: Lips have very thin skin and few oil glands, so they chap easily.
Hand emoji.Tooth: Enamel, the hardest substance in the body, coats each tooth.
